newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cetes rates fall on firm demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cetes rates fall on firm demand.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate fell again at the primary auction, as strong demand and lower secondary market rates helped push down rates across the yield curve, analysts said.
"The rates reacted to adjustments seen in the secondary market in the last few days," said Ricardo Vazquez, an analyst with Banco Union.
The rate on the bellwether 28-day paper fell 22 basis points to 23.06 percent on Tuesday. The 91-day Cetes rate fell 112 basis points to 25.63 percent.
In the 182-day term, the rate fell 83 basis points to 27.33 percent, while 364-day paper yielded 27.39 percent this week, compared to 28.03 percent for 343-day paper last week.
Demand rose to a sharp 17.44 billion pesos compared to 15.48 billion pesos the week before. The bid-to-cover ratio was 5.28 percent this week.
"It's likely there were foreigners in the auction. There was struggle for the paper, causing demand to rise," said Vazquez.
Overnight Cetes rates in the secondary market closed down 25 basis points to 22.75 percent on Tuesday.

"The declines (in the primary auction) were probably in response to strong domestic demand for Cetes during the Tuesday session, which pushed secondary rates down," MMS International said in a market report.
Analysts said that stability in the exchange rate helped the primary interest rates decline.
They added that real returns are now small and they do not rule out slight increases or an unchanged rate in the next few weeks.
